question: Which of the following correctly describes a feasible region in the context of Linear Programming?
explanation:
The feasible region is the set of all points that satisfy every constraint in the linear programming problem.

This includes all the linear inequalities along with the non-negativity restrictions. Graphically it is the common overlapping region determined by all constraints.

options.A: Any region determined by only the objective function
options.B: The region determined by the non-negativity constraints alone
options.C: The common region determined by all the constraints, including non-negativity
options.D: Only the region above the x-axis
